articles.summary: Rick Edwards, Luke Edwards and Clinton Morrison discuss the Premier League weekend.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 06 Sep 2026 , · 40 mins

Rick Edwards, Luke Edwards and Clinton Morrison discuss the latest Premier League weekend. Champions Arsenal maintained their perfect start to the season by coming from behind to beat Chelsea - can anyone stop them from defending their title? articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Are Blues short of midfield options despite £349m spent?
articles.summary: Chelsea ended Sunday's 2-1 defeat by champions Arsenal with two right-backs alongside each other in midfield - how did they get here?
articles.body:
Chelsea ended Sunday's 2-1 defeat by champions Arsenal with two players who began their careers as right-backs alongside each other in midfield.

After spending £349m during the summer transfer window, how did they reach that point?

It was Reece James, who began his career as a right-back, who failed to track captain Martin Odegaard as he scored Arsenal 's winner at Emirates Stadium.

In the build-up to his first defeat as Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso said he believes James can become one of the best midfielders in the world.

James performed well otherwise and spent almost half of last season playing in midfield.

But there are legitimate questions about Chelsea 's depth in that area after Malo Gusto replaced midfielder Romeo Lavia in the second half.

It was lax marking that led to Odegaard's winner, while a lack of creativity from the bench left Chelsea short as Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta's substitutes ultimately helped guide the hosts to victory.

" Chelsea don't have European football this season so they're playing less games and can concentrate on the Premier League. But the worry is you're finishing a game against the champions, and you've got two right-backs in midfield," Ashley Young told BBC Sport.

"You look at Lavia, who was injured a lot last season. The front line are going to send fear throughout the league but behind that you see the midfield and they're playing right-backs there.

"Teams will be seeing the game today, seeing that Chelsea will sit in there and get men behind the ball, but there's still spaces through the lines, and Arsenal found that out.

" Chelsea are giving up a lot of possession and they're playing counter-attacking football. Today there was probably only once with [Pedro] Neto down the right side when they capitalised on the counter."

The primary issue is the absence of midfielder Moises Caicedo.

The Ecuador international is out with an unspecified injury for an unknown period after breaking down just 11 minutes into a substitute appearance against Brighton last week.

It has left Alonso in almost uncharted territory for a Chelsea boss. Aside from suspensions, Caicedo had missed only two matches during the previous three seasons, through a knock and illness.

Asked about Caicedo, Alonso said: "Not longer term, but it is about assessing the risk. Probably last week we brought him back too early and I don't want to make the same mistake again."

It remains unclear whether Chelsea had concerns over Caicedo's fitness while pursuing several central midfielders on transfer deadline day.

Monaco pulled the plug on Chelsea 's £47m move for Lamine Camara at the last minute, leaving officials at Stamford Bridge furious.

Chelsea also had bids of up to £64m rejected for Bournemouth 's Alex Scott earlier in the summer and were prevented from signing France international Manu Kone after Roma head coach Gian Piero Gasperini blocked the move.

Chelsea said they pursued Camara because of a market opportunity, adding that they were satisfied with their summer business and retained faith in their current options.

That was despite selling Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint British-record fee of £125m on deadline day, without signing a direct replacement.

However, Caicedo's absence means he joins Jordan Henderson on the sidelines, with the England international still recovering from a broken arm suffered after falling over an advertising hoarding while an unused substitute at the World Cup.

Natural midfielder Valentin Barco, who joined from Strasbourg in the summer, has been overlooked in favour of Gusto in all three of Chelsea 's Premier League matches.

With Gusto starting in midfield, Chelsea recorded 25.6% possession in last weekend's 4-3 victory over Brighton , their lowest figure since records began in 2003-04.

If all of Chelsea 's midfield options are fit, and Caicedo's injury proves only minor, they should be able to cope with five midfielders in a season without midweek European football, as Alonso argued before the match.

Chelsea have leaned on their star attackers in Morgan Rogers, a resurgent Cole Palmer and the prolific Joao Pedro in their opening three matches.

Yet having conceded seven goals in three matches, Alonso said "we want to be tighter".

There was still plenty to admire about Chelsea 's performance.

Club-record signing Rogers scored again in the second minute, becoming the first Chelsea player to score or assist in each of the club's opening three Premier League matches of a season since Eden Hazard in 2018-19.

It was arguably one of Chelsea 's better performances against Arsenal during a run of 10 matches without a win against their London rivals.

There remains a 33-point gap to make up after Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League last season.

Alonso said after the match: "We came to win. We knew that we were not that far, but it went their way.

"It hurts, [we're] disappointed for sure. But this is the first defeat, this is going to be a long way and it doesn't have a big impact in our mood and in our mindset."

Arsenal remain the benchmark Chelsea are trying to reach. Although the Blues beat them to the signing of Rogers, they still trail the standard-setters in London and the Premier League.

It served to highlight that, despite already recruiting 10 first-team players during a busy summer, Chelsea 's failure to sign a midfielder on deadline day may have left them with a potential weakness.

Alonso described the summer as "phase one" earlier this week. If Caicedo's return does not resolve Chelsea 's midfield issues, the club may face questions over its decision not to sign a replacement for Fernandez before turning back to the market in January.

images.caption: Image caption, Reece James, right, has featured solely as a midfielder for manager Xabi Alonso in competitive matches this season

articles.title: Florida brings back banned 'Gator Bait' chant in season-opening win over FAU
articles.summary: Florida banned the "Gator Bait" chant in 2020 due to "horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase."
articles.body:
Florida's "Gator Bait" cheer returned on Saturday night at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium.

Roughly six years after the university banned their longtime chant due to "horrific historic racist imagery" that was associated with it, Florida brought back the cheer with the Gators band in the first quarter of their blowout 66-21 win over Florida Atlantic on Saturday.

The song and chant returning did not come as much of a surprise. The Florida band had been seen practicing the song ahead of the season-opener, and new Florida president Stuart Bell hinted in June that the chant could be making a return.

"I know there's a lot around the Gator Bait [cheer]," Bell said in June, via the Orlando Sentinel . "It's meaningful to the Gator family. I hope we're able to have some really great conversations around that."

Florida announced in 2020 , back when Kent Fuchs was the university's president, that the "Gator Bait" chant would no longer be led by the band at sporting events. The cheer and song had been popular at Florida events for decades, and is often accompanied by the Gator Chomp gesture.

Black babies were used as "alligator bait" in the late 1800s and early 1900s , and this became a popular artistic trope during the time.

"While I know of no evidence of racism associated with our 'Gator Bait' cheer at UF sporting events, there is horrific historic racist imagery associated with the phrase," Fuchs wrote in 2020. He also pointed to the murder of George Floyd while in police custody in Minneapolis that year when announcing the change, which was part of a larger national conversation about race.

Bell took over officially as Florida's president in July.

The Gators rolled to a 45-point win over FAU on Saturday in what was the first game under new head coach Jon Sumrall. Running back Jadan Baugh racked up 160 yards and three touchdowns in the win, and quarterback Aaron Philo threw for 275 yards and three touchdowns with an interception.

The Gators will host Campbell next on Saturday.

articles.title: Sinayoko stars as unbeaten Paris FC down Marseille
articles.summary: Lassine Sinayoko scored a hat-trick as Paris FC continued their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 season with a 3-2 victory at Marseille on Sunday.Rennes continu...
articles.body:
Lassine Sinayoko scored a hat-trick as Paris FC continued their unbeaten start to the Ligue 1 season with a 3-2 victory at Marseille on Sunday.

Liam Rosenior's Paris FC moved to second in the early table behind Monaco with seven points from their opening three games.

"For now, I just want to win the next match," said Paris coach Rosenior, bidding to rebuild his career after a disappointing spell at Chelsea.

"We believe we can achieve something in the long run by building things up. But in the short term, we have to keep working hard, stay humble and focus only on the next game."

Marseille, also under a new coach in Bruno Genesio, have suffered consecutive defeats after kicking off the campaign by thumping Strasbourg 4-0.

The visitors took the lead after just 25 seconds to silence the Velodrome crowd, as left-back Luca Koleosho got in behind and squared for Sinayoko to score.

Marseille levelled in the eighth minute when Amine Gouiri pounced on Adama Camara's mishit back pass to score his third league goal in as many games this season.

Sinayoko restored Paris FC's advantage 11 minutes later, heading in unmarked from a Pablo Pagis cross.

OM equalised again nine minutes into the second half, as Gouiri lashed in a close-range volley from a tight angle.

Marseille pushed forward in search of a winner, only to be caught out when Moses Simon's shot struck the arm of CJ Egan-Riley and PFC were awarded an 85th-minute penalty following a VAR review.

Sinayoko stepped up to complete his treble and ensure Rosenior's men extended their excellent start to the season going into next weekend's home game against Lyon.

Earlier, Strasbourg thumped Troyes 6-2 away from home as English winger Sam Amo-Ameyaw scored twice as a late substitute.

The 20-year-old Amo-Ameyaw, in his second season since joining from Southampton, scored in the 85th and 88th minutes.

Promoted Troyes had started their Ligue 1 campaign well with a win and a draw and took the lead on nine minutes through Antoine Mille.

One of Strasbourg's summer signings, Jacobo Ortega, tapped home a simple equaliser before the break for his first league goal since joining from Real Madrid.

The floodgates then opened, as the visitors produced a display of excellent finishing.

Two more summer recruits, Diogo Sousa and American starlet Giovanni Reyna, and loan signing Conrad Harder, also scored.

Strasbourg face league leaders Monaco next weekend.

Rennes continued their unbeaten start to the campaign with a 2-1 victory at Angers.

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain lost 2-1 at home to Monaco on Friday and are still without a win.

Lille won away at Toulouse on Thursday and Lens fell to a second straight defeat, losing 1-0 at home to Lorient.

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Alexander Isak, Ezri Konsa, Tyrick Mitchell, Harvey Barnes
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Tell us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

David Raya ( Arsenal ): Huge saves, again. It's why he's the best goalkeeper in the league. He keeps just coming up with big moments.

Ezri Konsa ( Arsenal ): Solid performance. He comes in again and just makes that massive tackle on Morgan Rogers. I think he slots into what is an already incredible Arsenal team. I can see a position now that they just can't live without him, he'll have to play right-back when everybody comes fit and available.

Ronald Araujo ( Liverpool ): I've given him a bit of stick for his games at Barcelona and his ability to not defend properly, because he's normally the one who's really aggressive. But I have to give it to him, he's been really good for Liverpool and played at right-back in that situation.

Tyrick Mitchell ( Crystal Palace ): Two goals from left-back. He deserves to be in any team of the week. He came off as well, but he's just Mr Consistent. He's never really spoken about enough.

Harvey Barnes ( Newcastle ): Gets a goal. Good finish into that far corner as well. He's been excellent and not spoken about a lot. Anthony Elanga and all the others get the headlines, but Barnes has been fantastic.

Martin Odegaard ( Arsenal ): Captain, leader and a massive winner. It's just one of those moments where you just think, how did they talk about getting rid of Odegaard? It's scary.

Cody Gakpo ( Liverpool ): Two goals created from midfield. Imagine thinking you're playing for Spurs and then for Man City, and then somehow you have to stay at Liverpool and compose yourself, and still perform.

Cesar Palacios ( Fulham ) and Vitaly Janelt ( Brentford ): Both very similar: solid and get the job done. They don't really get noticed in games unless they score, but if you're watching and you've played the game, you know these two are really important.

Alexander Isak ( Liverpool ): The guy they keep telling you isn't good. They say last year he wasn't good, even though he had two injuries, one being a broken leg. This season, he doesn't score in one game against Newcastle and, 'oh, he's not good enough, he's bottled it'. Just remember, someone tipped him for the Golden Boot.

Kai Havertz ( Arsenal ): The best striker for Arsenal , hands down. They keep telling us that Gyokeres will come good, but Havertz is their best striker. He proves it week in, week out. He's the best footballer they've got, and also their best finisher.

David Moyes ( Everton ): Bad transfer window, loses his attacking options and still delivers a result.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza: "No podemos defender el área así en la última jugada"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Sevilla analizó el empate con el Espanyol y volvió a lamentar la polémica arbitral
articles.summary: El entrenador del Sevilla analizó el empate con el Espanyol y volvió a lamentar la polémica arbitral
articles.body: Luis García Plaza atendió a los medios después del empate del Sevilla en su visita al Espanyol, un encuentro que el conjunto nervionense tuvo que afrontar durante muchos minutos en inferioridad numérica por la expulsión de Arouna Sangante (1-1). "Nos estamos complicando mucho en las decisiones. Sangante da a la pelota, no es roja, no hay ninguna interpretación. Después de darle a la pelota, ¿qué hace el jugador? Va al suelo, da al balón y no puede quitarse de en medio, no puede desaparecer. Hay demasiadas complicaciones, a veces a favor, a veces en contra. Esta vez todos coinciden en que no es roja., todos los que me comentan en el campo", inició el técnico madrileño. Charla con el árbitro: "No me ha explicado las jugadas de los goles. Sí que ha venido porque cuando me ha enseñado tarjeta amarilla, me ha explicado la expulsión. Pero los goles no lo sé, no los he visto". Análisis del partido: "Creo que fue un partido muy rico. Nos han superado al principio, pero después hemos ajustado muy bien a partir del cuarto de hora, donde creo que teníamos el partido controlado. Con diez creo que hemos hecho un partidazo porque no solo es el gol, es que nos hemos plantado delante del portero. Ha tenido Lucas una jugada de Guridi que lo ha dejado solo y podíamos haber hecho el 0-1 antes. El gol nos lo meten de una manera rara, no podemos defender el área así en la última jugada y es un error que tenemos que corregir". Empieza otra liga: "Siempre digo que los puntos valen igual la primera que cualquier otra jornada. Hemos conseguido siete, nos ha pasado de todo a favor y en contra en los partidos, situaciones chulas de ver y un equipo entretenido. Cuando termina el mercado mis jugadores son los mejores. Estamos viendo un Sevilla que compite en cada partido. Incluso el otro día cuando Atlético de Madrid nos supera 0-3 en la primera parte y en la segunda competimos muy bien. Espero que eso nunca se pierda". Fofana y Stassin: "Fofana llevaba desde el 1 de febrero sin jugar 90 minutos, pero creo que es un jugador que nos va a dar mucho poderío físico y una traslación de campo buenísima. Lucas yo creo que se va a entender bien. Incluso en algún momento puede jugar con Isaac o con Robbie, pero es que llevan pocos entrenos. Y a Félix no lo he podido sacar por la expulsión. Al final todos son importantes".

images.caption: Luis García, en rueda de prensa. EFE

articles.title: Manolo González, sobre el tanto anulado a El Hilai: "Nadie lo entiende muy bien"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Espanyol asegura que les afectó más esta situación que el tanto de Stassin en el minuto 85
articles.summary: El técnico del Espanyol asegura que les afectó más esta situación que el tanto de Stassin en el minuto 85
articles.body: El entrenador del Espanyol, Manolo González, ha apuntado, tras empatar contra el Sevilla en el RCDE Stadium, que "nadie entiende muy bien por qué han anulado" el 1-0 de Omar El Hilali y ha reconocido que "llega un punto" en el que "no sabemos muy bien qué es o no fuera de juego". El técnico, en rueda de prensa, ha desvelado que la explicación para anular el gol de Omar El Hilali por fuera de juego del ariete blanquiazul Marcos Fernández es "porque estaba en la trayectoria y ya está". González ha apuntado que incluso en situaciones similares "pinta de un modo diferente de una semana a otra". El preparador ha confesado que el gol anulado a Omar El Hilali por fuera de juego ha afectado más que el 0-1 de Stassin en el 85: "Sí, porque es una jugada de mucho mérito de Javi Hernández, que saca un centro muy bien, y Omar llega muy bien. El partido se te pone de cara con el 1-0 y ellos ya se tienen que abrir". Respecto a la expulsión de Sangante en el minuto 58, el gallego ha asegurado que es "clara". "Por mucho que toque el balón, toca al jugador, porque sino Roberto Fernández se queda delante del portero", ha detallado. González ha aplaudido el rendimiento de Marcos Fernández, autor del gol del empate en el minuto 98. "Le hemos puesto por este motivo, queríamos dos delanteros. El cambio iba igual antes de la expulsión de Sangante. Queríamos más presencia en el área y Marcos te la puede dar", ha desgranado. Por otra parte, González ha apuntado que el equipo ha tenido "quizá demasiada calma" en la primera parte. "La pelota debería haber ido más rápido. Pienso que deberíamos haber movido más rápido al rival", ha analizado, insistiendo en la importancia de incrementar la circulación del balón. El entrenado ha confesado que es "urgente" solucionar los problemas de la salida: "Una cosa es querer jugar, ser un equipo que proponga y tener la pelota y otra es equivocarnos como hemos hecho hoy. Tengo bastante claro lo que hay que tocar a nivel ofensivo esta semana, ya".

articles.title: El Real Murcia disfruta, golea e ilusiona a su afición
articles.standfirst: Marcaron Joel Jorquera por partida doble, Javi Moreno y Cristo Romero para que los de la capital del Segura comanden la tabla con seis puntos
articles.summary: Marcaron Joel Jorquera por partida doble, Javi Moreno y Cristo Romero para que los de la capital del Segura comanden la tabla con seis puntos
articles.body: El Real Murcia dejó claro en la segunda jornada del Grupo 2 de Primera Federación que sus intenciones para el curso 26/27 son de altura. Los de la capital del Segura firmaron un contundente 4-0 ante un CD Teruel que se marchó de tierras murcianas sin sumar y con la sensación de haber sido superado en todas las facetas del juego. Con esta goleada, el conjunto grana se consolida en lo más alto de su grupo con pleno de puntos, mientras que el bloque turolense encaja un serio correctivo que le empuja hacia las profundidades de la tabla. FICHA TÉCNICA Real Murcia, 4: Dani Jiménez; Jorge Mier, Héctor Pérez, Rojas, Cristo Romero (Mounir Errahaly, min.72); Óscar Gil (Moyita, min.72), Javi Mier (Chema Núñez, min.61), Álvaro Bustos (Joao Pedro, min.61); Javi Moreno, Joel Jorquera y Flakus (Álvaro Giménez, min.78). Club Deportivo Teruel, 0: Zarco; Llácer, Goyo Medina (Romera, min.46), Álvaro López, Pablo Felipe (Sesé, min.46), Joserra; Haritz Albisua, Relu, Redón (Moraitis, min.58); Edu Gallardo y Sergio Moreno (Carlos Igual, min.72). Goles: 1-0, Min.17: Joel Jorquera. 2-0, Min.54: Javi Moreno. 3-0, Min.69: Cristo Romero. 4-0, Min.87: Jorquera. Árbitro: Sergio Escriche Guzmán, del comité valenciano. Mostró la tarjeta amarilla a los locales Javier Mier (min.52) y Mounir Errahaly (min.80) y a los visitantes Álvaro López (min.47) y Romera (min.85). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la segunda jornada de Liga en el grupo 2 de la Primera RFEF de fútbol que se disputó en el estadio Enrique Roca de Murcia ante unos 15.746 espectadores. Antes del inicio del encuentro se guardó un minuto de silencio por los aficionados fallecidos desde el final de la pasada temporada y también en memoria de Francisco Sánchez Ruiz, padre del director general de Deportes de la Comunidad Autónoma, Francisco Javier Sánchez López. Un partido encarrilado desde el arranque El Murcia no necesitó demasiado para poner las cosas de cara. En el minuto 17, Joel Jorquera abría el marcador para desatar la fiesta en las gradas y establecer el 1-0 con el que se llegaría al descanso. El centrocampista, uno de los grandes protagonistas de la tarde, marcó la pauta de un encuentro que el equipo local siempre tuvo bajo control. El técnico visitante intentó reaccionar en el intermedio con un doble cambio nada más comenzar la segunda mitad: Mario Sesé por Goyo Medina y Miguel Romera por Pablo Felipe, en busca de aire fresco y una reacción que nunca llegó. Al contrario, el Murcia apretó todavía más el acelerador. En el minuto 54, Javier Moreno amplió distancias para hacer el 2-0 y encaminar definitivamente los tres puntos. La sentencia llegó en el tramo final. En el minuto 69, Cristo Romero transformó en gol una asistencia de un Jorquera pletórico para poner el 3-0. Y ya en el 87, el propio Joel Jorquera cerró su cuenta particular y la goleada con el definitivo 4-0, firmando un doblete que lo convierte en el nombre propio de la jornada en Nueva Condomina. Jorquera, dueño y señor del partido Si hubo un futbolista que iluminó el choque, ese fue Joel Jorquera. El '19' grana no solo se marchó con dos tantos en su haber, sino que además repartió la asistencia del tercer gol a Cristo Romero. Participación directa en tres de los cuatro goles de su equipo: una actuación completa que resume a la perfección la tarde de dominio local. El propio Cristo Romero, defensa de perfil ofensivo, aportó su granito de arena sumándose a la fiesta goleadora, un detalle que ilustra la profundidad con la que el Murcia atacó por todos los frentes. Javier Moreno, por su parte, aprovechó su oportunidad para dejar su firma en el marcador y redondear un rendimiento coral. El entrenador local incluso pudo permitirse el lujo de dar rodaje a jugadores como Chema Núñez, Sergio Moyita, Mounir Errahaly y el veterano Álvaro Giménez, que entraron desde el banquillo con el partido ya resuelto y la mente puesta en administrar el esfuerzo. El Teruel, sin respuesta y sin pegada El cuadro aragonés se marchó de Murcia sin haber sido capaz de generar peligro suficiente para inquietar la portería defendida por Dani Jiménez. La imagen del Teruel fue la de un equipo desbordado, incapaz de encontrar el camino hacia la portería rival y castigado cada vez que el Murcia decidió pisar el acelerador. El único apunte disciplinario reseñable en el conjunto visitante fueron las cartulinas amarillas que vieron Álvaro López en el minuto 52 y Miguel Romera en el 85. Por parte local, vieron amonestación Javi Mier (52') y Mounir Errahaly (81'), en un partido que, más allá del abultado marcador, no tuvo grandes momentos de tensión: no hubo expulsiones y el ritmo lo marcó siempre el equipo grana. La clasificación: Murcia arriba, Teruel en zona de alarma El resultado tiene una lectura clara en la tabla del Grupo 2. El Real Murcia encabeza la clasificación con 6 puntos de 6 posibles, dos victorias en dos jornadas y un balance goleador de 6 goles a favor por solo 1 en contra, la mejor diferencia del grupo (+5). Comparte el pleno de puntos con el Villarreal B U23, pero le supera por diferencia de goles gracias precisamente a esta goleada. En el lado opuesto de la balanza, el CD Teruel se hunde hasta la 17ª posición con un único punto. Los números son elocuentes: dos partidos disputados, ninguna victoria, un empate, una derrota y, sobre todo, 0 goles a favor por 4 en contra, la peor diferencia de gol de todo el grupo (-4). El conjunto aragonés todavía no ha visto puerta en lo que va de campeonato, una estadística que enciende las primeras alarmas en un tramo del curso en el que empezar a sumar y a marcar resulta clave para no descolgarse. Un aviso a navegantes Con apenas dos jornadas disputadas, es pronto para sacar conclusiones definitivas, pero el mensaje del Real Murcia no puede ser más contundente. El bloque grana combina solidez defensiva —solo un gol encajado en dos partidos— con una pegada que ya ha dejado seis dianas, y en Joel Jorquera parece haber encontrado a un futbolista capaz de decidir partidos por sí solo. La afición de Nueva Condomina se frota las manos. El CD Teruel, en cambio, tendrá que hacer autocrítica y buscar cuanto antes ese primer gol que se le resiste. La categoría no perdona los arranques titubeantes, y el correctivo murciano debe servir de revulsivo para un equipo que aún tiene toda una temporada por delante para enderezar el rumbo.

articles.title: El Zamora se atasca en el Ruta de la Plata
articles.standfirst: Iago Indias igualó antes del descanso el tanto inicial de Anai, pero Santana castigó a los rojiblancos en el minuto 82 para dejar al equipo con un punto de seis posibles
articles.summary: Iago Indias igualó antes del descanso el tanto inicial de Anai, pero Santana castigó a los rojiblancos en el minuto 82 para dejar al equipo con un punto de seis posibles
articles.body: El fútbol tiene esa costumbre cruel de castigar al que perdona. El Zamora CF lo comprobó este domingo en un partido que tuvo en sus manos, al menos anímicamente, y que terminó cayendo del lado de una UD Logroñés fría, resolutiva y perfecta en el arranque de la temporada. El conjunto riojano se impuso por 1-2 en la segunda jornada del Grupo 1 de la Primera Federación, ante 3.097 espectadores, con un gol de Ismael Santana en el minuto 83 que rompió el equilibrio y firmó el segundo triunfo consecutivo del equipo visitante. FICHA TÉCNICA Zamora: Iker Piedra, Moreno (Gorjón, 70), Luengo, Indias, Vergés, Fabi, Isiah (Juanje, 70), Ramos, Mascaró (Sancho, 57), Izán /Eri Gómez, 77) y Losada (Carbonell, 77) UD Logroñés: Fermín, Navarro, Bolo, Cabetas, Camacho (Barandalla, 77), Zabala (Asenjo, 63), Marí (Maroto, 22), Issman (Rivero, 63), Santana, Anai y Baselga (Amigo, 63) Goles: 0-1, m. 41. Anai; 1-1, m. 45+, Indias. 1-2, m. 81, Santana Árbitro: Guillermo Conejero. Amonestó al local Fabi; y a los blanquirrojos Navarro, Maroto y Bolo. Incidencias: Segunda en Primera Federación. Ruta de la Plata. El desarrollo: dos golpes antes y después del descanso El Logroñés dio el primer aviso convertido en gol. En el minuto 42, Anai Morales culminó una jugada asistida por Mikel Zabala para adelantar a los suyos (0-1) justo cuando el primer tiempo agonizaba. La ventaja, sin embargo, duró apenas tres minutos: en el 45, Iago Indias —central del Zamora— apareció para empatar el encuentro sin asistencia registrada y mandar a los dos equipos al descanso con un 1-1 que reactivaba las esperanzas locales. La segunda mitad se convirtió en un pulso de relevos. Ambos entrenadores movieron el banquillo con generosidad: el Zamora dio entrada a Jaime Sancho, Aleix Gorjón, Juanje, Javier Carbonell y Eric Gómez, mientras que el Logroñés respondió con Quique Rivero, David Amigo, Ibai Asenjo y, de forma determinante, Miguel Barandalla, que saltó al terreno en el minuto 79. Fue precisamente Barandalla quien decidió el partido. Cuatro minutos después de su entrada, en el 83, asistió a Ismael Santana para el 1-2 definitivo. Un cambio que salió redondo y que dejó al Zamora sin margen para reaccionar en el tramo final. Un partido marcado por las tarjetas visitantes... y por un cambio forzado El Logroñés acumuló amonestaciones a lo largo de la segunda mitad —David Navarro (56'), Mario Maroto (60') y Bolo (67')—, señal de un equipo que no dudó en frenar las transiciones locales cuando fue necesario. Por parte del Zamora, vio cartulina Juanje (74'), poco después de haber entrado al campo. El encuentro tuvo además un condicionante temprano para los riojanos: en el minuto 23, el capitán Miguel Marí tuvo que retirarse por lesión, obligando a un cambio prematuro con la entrada de Mario Maroto. Pese a perder a su brazalete tan pronto, el conjunto visitante supo reordenarse sin perder el control del choque desde su estructura de 4-2-3-1, frente al 4-4-2 planteado por el Zamora. Los protagonistas Ismael Santana se erigió en el hombre del partido. El delantero, el jugador de mayor valor de mercado del once titular visitante, resolvió con oficio la ocasión que le brindó Barandalla para sumar su gol y darle tres puntos de oro a su equipo. Anai Morales, autor del primer tanto y también uno de los futbolistas más cotizados del once riojano, confirmó su peso en la medular con una acción decisiva antes del descanso. En el Zamora, el central Iago Indias fue el único que logró superar al portero Fermín Sobrón, con un gol que mantuvo con vida a los suyos hasta el tramo final. El capitán local, Carlos Ramos, no pudo llevar a su equipo más allá del empate momentáneo. Lo que dice la clasificación El resultado consolida a la UD Logroñés en la zona alta del Grupo 1: con dos victorias en dos jornadas, los riojanos suman 6 puntos y ocupan la tercera posición, únicamente por detrás de Real Unión Club y Pontevedra CF —ambos también con pleno—, quedando descolgados por diferencia de goles (4 a favor y 2 en contra). Un arranque impecable para un equipo que ha ganado sus dos primeros compromisos. Muy distinto es el panorama para el Zamora CF. La derrota lo deja en la decimotercera plaza con apenas 1 punto, fruto de un empate y una derrota en sus dos primeros partidos, con dos goles a favor y tres en contra. Un balance que enciende las primeras alarmas en un grupo tan igualado en su parte media que cualquier tropiezo penaliza en la tabla. El conjunto zamorano necesita reaccionar pronto para no verse arrastrado hacia la zona de peligro, en la que ya asoman equipos como Real Avilés, Unión Deportiva Ourense y Unionistas de Salamanca CF, todavía sin puntuar. Conclusión El 1-2 de Zamora encierra una lección clásica: el Logroñés no fue necesariamente superior durante 90 minutos, pero sí fue más eficaz en los momentos clave y más acertado en la gestión del banquillo. El acierto de Barandalla como revulsivo y la definición de Santana marcaron la diferencia entre sumar y sumar de tres. Para el Zamora, el gol de Iago Indias no fue suficiente premio a un empate que se le escapó en el tramo final. Dos caminos opuestos tras dos jornadas: uno instalado en la élite del grupo, el otro obligado ya a mirar hacia arriba.

articles.title: Women’s U-20 World Cup ultimate guide: Team insight, players to watch and predicted finishes
articles.summary: The U-20 World Cup is the top competition in the women’s youth game. USWNT manager Emma Hayes called it ‘the biggest platform for young players to play in’.T...
articles.body:
The U-20 World Cup is the top competition in the women's youth game. USWNT manager Emma Hayes called it 'the biggest platform for young players to play in'.

Teams who do well here often go on to dominate at senior level. Spain won the U-20 title in 2022, then won the senior World Cup the following year with several of the same players.

The tournament runs from September 5th-27th, hosted across four Polish cities — Łódź, Bielsko-Biała, Katowice and Sosnowiec.

With the action now underway, here is the ultimate guide to the tournament broken down by team, including players you should keep an eye on.

Poland will make their tournament debut as the hosts. Their previous competitive fixture was an impressive 2-0 win over Mexico. The team is coached by Marcin Kasprowicz, who holds a PhD. His thesis examined the game structure at the 2007 FIFA Women's World Cup.

Polish women's football has seen a massive rise in recent years, with the senior team qualifying for UEFA Women's EURO 2025 for the first time. Barcelona's Ewa Pajor is a huge icon forPolish football.

Kasprowicz said: "It's a special time everything we do now is for the development of Polish women's football. The Polish FA has special projects to develop young players, like the Young Eagles Academy."

Argentina have qualified for the U-20 Women's World Cup for the fifth time. They are one of four South American teams to have qualified. While Argentina are not as prominent in the women's game as they are in the men's, they will want to make their mark.

They impressed in the group phase of the recent South American Under-20 Women's Football Championship, beating both Ecuador and Brazil. Form dipped in the final round, though, where they lost to Ecuador and were beaten 4-0 by Brazil. Their mixed results make the team hard to predict, but on their day they can be unstoppable.

Benin were one of four African qualifiers for the global final. They beat Guinea, Egypt and Côte d'Ivoire along the way, delivering some promising results. It is the first time that the YoungAmazons have qualified for the competition.

One to watch is 15-year-old Romaine Gandonou. Gandonou was African qualifying's top scorer with 14 goals. The young star has already featured for the senior team and has attractedattention from both PSG and Barcelona.

Mexico have qualified for the tournament for the 12th time. They secured their spot by reaching the final of the 2025 Concacaf Women's U-20 Championship, where they were beaten3-2 by Canada. The team has reached the quarter-finals four times before, most recently in 2022.

With the Mexican FA's focus on the youth set-up, most of the players play in Mexico's top flight and have plenty of experience at a high level. However, they are up against some toughcompetition and may struggle to progress out of the group.

Brazil have never missed a U-20 Women's World Cup and have finished third twice before. They secured their place by winning the South American U-20 Women's FootballChampionship.

The squad recently played the U-20 USWNT, losing 2-0 and drawing 0-0. With the US being one of the tournament favourites, this has given them confidence they can go toe to toe with the giants.

Canada are a quality side with good experience. The young Canadians earned a spot by winning the 2025 Concacaf Women's U-20 Championship, beating the US and Mexico along theway. They have struggled in recent matches, losing to group-mates England and Brazil and drawing with Japan.

In this group, every match matters, and they may not make it out of the group.

England's squad is stacked with WSL, NWSL and Champions League experience. They have played seven fixtures in the build-up, with mixed but promising results. England's best finishremains 2018, when they reached the semi-final before losing 2-0 to Japan. They then beat France on penalties to finish third overall.

Manager Lydia Bedford is confident, saying: "By the time we get to the World Cup, we'll have played four non-European opponents since June, and I think that puts us in a really positiveplace."

With hard work and a little luck, England may be able to go far.

Tanzania were one of four African qualifiers. The Tanzanians edged Cameroon on away goals (3-3 agg.) to qualify. It is their first time qualifying for the tournament, and the squad has not had much international experience.

With the quality in this group, they are likely to struggle.

Ecuador will feature in their first ever U-20 Women's World Cup. They struggled initially in the South American Under-20 Women's Football Championship, before winning astring of games to become the second South American team to qualify, behind Brazil.

They ended the tournament as runners-up, their best ever finish, and go into the World Cup full of confidence. With momentum behind them, they have enough quality to spring a surprise in the knockout rounds.

France are looking to make serious headway in this competition. They reached the European U-19 Championship final in 2025, losing to Spain. The French side were runners-up at theWorld Cup in 2016 and want to go one better this time.

Their squad has plenty of talent and experience, such as Maeline Mendy, who is a regular for Paris FC and has been attracting serious attention from across Europe.

Ghana have featured in the tournament seven times before but have never made it out of the group stage. The Black Princesses made it to the tournament by beating Uganda in theplay-offs.

The squad have been training hard since qualifying, with an initial 45-player squad battling it out for a place in the final selection.

South Korea qualified by reaching the semi-finals of the U-20 Women's Asian Cup. They have serious pedigree in the tournament, having featured eight times previously and finishing third in 2010. While they have struggled more in recent years, they are ready to make it deep into the tournament.

Italy are featuring at the tournament for the first time. They have had mixed results in the lead-up, including a 1-1 draw against Sweden and a 5-1 loss to the Netherlands.Italy will have to sharpen up fast if they want a chance against the likes of Japan and the United States.

Japan booked their spot at Poland 2026 by winning the U-20 Women's Asian Cup. They will be looking to win their second U-20 World Cup trophy this time out.In preparation, Japan played some of the top contenders in friendlies. They beat England 1-0 and drew 2-2 with Canada, giving them good experience against teams outside Asia.

New Zealand are regulars in the competition, having appeared ten times. They qualified by winning the OFC U-19 Women's Championship, defeating New Caledonia 3-0 in the final. The squad will be confident going into the tournament after the OFC win.

Their group is tough and they have limited experience against teams outside Oceania, but they have enough about them to cause an upset.

The United States have not only qualified for every edition of the tournament since it began in 2002, they have also won it the most times, joint with Germany and North Korea. However, they have not lifted the trophy since 2012.

The US stars will have added motivation, as USWNT senior manager Emma Hayes highly rates the competition and will be there in person to scout young talent.

Colombia were hosts of the last U-20 World Cup, which helped to promote the women's game in the South American country. Their best previous result was fourth in 2010.

In the lead-up to the tournament, Colombia beat the United States 1-0 and lost to England on penalties after holding them to a 0-0 draw. This experience and confidence will do wonders for a team hoping to go deep in the competition.

Costa Rica have qualified for the World Cup for the third time in a row. The last time Las Ticas faced group-mates North Korea, they lost 9-0. Manager Patricia Aguilar is excited to show how far the team have come in the two years since that result, and they have real talent to back it up, with players already part of the senior set-up.

North Korea come into this tournament as reigning champions, having lifted the trophy for a third time in 2024. The North Koreans won all seven of their games at the last tournamentwithout needing extra time.

The team also finished runners-up in the recent U-20 Asian Cup. They will be hoping to retain their crown this time out.

Portugal qualified for their first ever U-20 World Cup after finishing runners-up in their U-19 Euros group last year.

They have had mixed results in the lead-up to the tournament, including a 2-0 loss to England in their final warm-up game. They are drawn in a tough group, but have some quality goalscorers in the squad who could make the difference.

China have reached the final twice before but have never won the U-20 World Cup. They qualified via an impressive Asian Cup campaign, where they ultimately lost to Japan, who wenton to win the tournament.

They have a tough group, but their pedigree and depth of talent give them a real chance of reaching the knockout stage.

New Caledonia have qualified for the tournament for the first time, having reached the OFC final, where they lost to New Zealand. The small country has a population of just under 300,000, making them the smallest nation to qualify.

They will likely struggle but it is a great experience for the team to play at such a high level.

Nigeria are seasoned regulars at the U-20 World Cup, having never failed to qualify. The Falconets are truly the giants of African football, and they have finished runners-up in thecompetition twice.

There is plenty of international experience in the squad, with some players already playing in the top divisions across Europe.

Spain may not have the history of some of the other teams, but they do have the pedigree and one of the best youth development systems in the world.

They won the competition for the first time in 2022, and it is no surprise that the senior squad also won the World Cup in Australia and New Zealand for the first time a year later.Spain won the U-19 Euros last year, and most of the squad from that win will be playing at the World Cup. Their squad had a couple of big wins in the lead-up to the tournament, including a 6-0 win against the Netherlands.

articles.title: Angel Reese's defense leads USA vs Italy FIBA World Cup winners, losers
articles.summary: The USA got all it could handle from Italy in group play on Sunday at the FIBA Women's World Cup, escaping with a win. Here are the winners and loses.
articles.body:
The USA women's basketball team continued its run at the FIBA World Cup, holding off Italy, 55-52, in their second game of group play on Sunday, Sept. 6, in Berlin, Germany.

The Americans, who have won four consecutive World Cup titles, won their 32nd consecutive game in the tournament but this one did not come easily. It was their smallest margin of victory since 1979 and lowest shooting percentage (29%) from the floor ever.

"Every single one of those wins came hard. ... and we understand that," said USA coach Kara Lawson, whose team advanced to the quarterfinals with the victory. "You have to have great respect for who you play, you have to prepare in a way to win. And so, it's supposed to be challenging, and we're supposed to have moments where we're not at our best.

"And the teams that can persevere through that and have a resilient mindset are the ones that are able to win. If you're fortunate enough at the end of the tournament to be the winner, that's why it's so satisfying."

Team USA had faced off against Italy in March at the World Cup qualifying tournament in Puerto Rico. Team USA defeated Italy 93-59 behind Kahleah Copper's game-high 15 points, one of five Americans to score in double digits in the March 14 win.

Only one player was in double digits on Sunday: Jackie Young, who scored 10 points to lead the Americans.

Here are the winners and losers for Sunday's game between the USA and Italy:

Team USA women ready to make noise at FIBA World Cup

If there is a clutch basket to be had, Chelsea Gray typically nails it. Gray, like much of Team USA, did not have a great shooting day. Before her eventual game-winning shot, she was 1-of-5 from the floor. However, when the pressure was on, and the United States needed to put some distance between itself and Italy, the veteran guard delivered.

Gray drew a timely charge around the 3-minute mark to shift the momentum, and then sank a gritty two-point jumper with 1:07 left on the clock to put the U.S. up 55-50. The shot couldn't have come at a better time. It forced Italy to take a timeout. The United States was able to walk away with a win thanks for Gray's heroics.

"The shot Chelsea took was a big momentum changing play," Lawson said. "It was an incredible winning play by Gray there."

While Team USA struggled to make a shot, Reese used her defensive prowess to lock down Italy. She had two blocks, a steal and three rebounds. Reese also scored eight points, making all four free-throws and two field goals.

"She comes into the game, and she plays with great energy, and she competes," Team USA coach Kara Lawson said. "She scores, she rebounds, she plays with great pace. It's what you want in a player, in a young player, to come in and do that. And so that's what I appreciate more about her. She finds a way to make an impact."

The Italians held the American to a FIBA Women's World Cup worst 28.6% shooting from the field. After opening the game in man-to-man, Italy was down 19-8 at the end of the first quarter. They switched to a zone and caused many problems for the U.S., playing extremely physical basketball, especially inside.

"We wanted to break their rhythm because when they get their rhythm, it's really unstoppable," said Italy forward Cecilia Zandalasini, who had 14 points and seven rebounds. "We try with the zone, we try different matchups, we try some switches and ... did a great, great job on their post player because I know they want to put the ball inside it."

The United States shot 10-for-35 in the paint and 1-for-12 from 3-point land.

2026 WNBA season is underway. See photos from the league's 30th year

Team USA might want to review Sunday's film and then never speak of it again. It was that ugly. It was particularly bad on two-point field goals. The United States was 15-for-44 on 2-pointers and missed more than 20 shots in the paint alone. That just can't happen. Full credit goes to Italy for packing the paint and applying pressure, causing a lot missed shots.

"We got quality looks against their zone and against their man in the paint, exactly where we wanted," Lawson said. "We just missed them. We missed the layups, and so, hopefully, moving forward, we can finish a few more."

The U.S. survived after an awful shooting night. What saved them? Getting to the free-throw line, where it finished 22-for-30. Still, that won't happen every game.

"Obviously, Italy really kind of mucked up the game for us a little bit, and it made it hard on us to score," Breanna Stewart said. "Tough team ... This is a tough tournament, but we all really acknowledge that."

In the opening game of group play, the U.S. shot 12-for-32 from 3-point range in a convincing victory over China . They got hot from beyond the arc in the first half and never looked back.

That was not the case vs. Italy. The U.S. was 1-of-12 from 3. Caitlin Clark was 0-for-3 and Rhyne Howard and Kahleah Cooper were both 0-for-2 from behind the arc. Paige Bueckers hit the lone 3-pointer, with 1:45 to go in the third quarter.

"That was a game plan, and we played with our heart," Italy coach Andrea Capobianco said. "That was the key actually.

"We just gotta keep going. We have another very important game tomorrow. Now, we showed what we're capable of, but we want to keep going and not just stopping here and just lose our head on this game. It's still a very, very long tournament."

Team USA's mystifying field goal problems

Team USA having multiple players without a field goal during a World Cup game is nearly unthinkable. But that's what happened Sunday.

At one point, there were four players without a field goal. Breanna Stewart, who was 0-for-8 late, finally got one to go at the 3:20 mark of the fourth, which turned out to be pivotal in the victory. Guards Caitlin Clark (0-for 6), Kahleah Copper (0-for-4) and Sonia Citron (0-for-1) did not make a basket from the field.

To be fair to the group, they had a lot of shots hit the rim and bounce out. The U.S. will have trouble competing when its stars can't find the net.

The USA will need to find out quickly how to get them going again,. The Americans play Czechia on Monday, Sept. 7 after less than a 24-hour turnaround.
authors: Heather Burns and Meghan L. Hall, USA TODAY

articles.title: 🎥 Flamengo celebrate! Botafogo and Palmeiras play out a draw
articles.summary: There has been a change at the top of the 2026 Brasileirão after 18 rounds.After seeing Flamengo do its part, Palmeiras faced Botafogo on Sunday night (6).An...
articles.body:
There has been a change at the top of the 2026 Brasileirão after 18 rounds.

After seeing Flamengo do its part, Palmeiras faced Botafogo on Sunday night (6).

And they were held to a 0-0 draw with Glorioso at Nilton Santos.

A result that confirmed Rubro-Negro in first place.

The match was valid for round 26 of the competition.

And it featured Carlo Ancelotti in attendance three days before the national team call-up for the next FIFA international window.

Botafogo had the better start. They moved the ball well.

And the crowd was getting on Marlon Freitas and Barboza's backs.

Palmeiras gradually found their footing as the minutes went by.

There was almost a penalty in the 24th minute.

The appeals were for a red card, but Marçal was shown yellow after bringing down Andreas almost inside the box.

Botafogo's chance before the break came after the No. 10 put Villalba in a great position.

But the Uruguayan forward failed to make it count.

The second half also saw Palmeiras with more possession and attacking play.

Maurício would have scored in the 12th minute if not for Gabriel Batista.

The substitutions made by Bellão and Abel did not have the desired effect.

Palmeiras even ended up with one man less. But Barboza's sending-off after catching Huguinho came only in the final minute.

Botafogo moved to 31 points after going five matches without a win.

They will return to Brasileirão action next Saturday (12), when they host Red Bull Bragantino.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, reached 53 points. Confirming Flamengo at the top, after they had reached 54 earlier.

Their next league match will also be on Saturday (12). Nubank Parque will host the Choque-Rei.

Before that, however, they have the first leg of the Copa Libertadores quarter-finals.

They will face LDU next Wednesday (9), also in front of their home fans.

articles.title: Different names execute Urs Fischer’s ‘principles’ as Mainz overwhelm Hamburg
articles.summary: Mainz 05 head coach Urs Fischer praised his squad’s ability to maintain its tactical principles despite significant personnel changes after Sunday’s emphatic...
articles.body:
Mainz 05 head coach Urs Fischer praised his squad's ability to maintain its tactical principles despite significant personnel changes after Sunday's emphatic 0-5 Bundesliga victory away at Hamburger SV. Fischer's "Nullfünter" produced a scoreline worthy of their name on the second matchday of the 2026/27 Bundesliga.

The Rheinhessen overwhelmed Hamburg from the opening stages at the Volksparkstadion, with Sheraldo Becker scoring once and setting up two more goals before Phillip Tietz completed a brace. Former HSV attacker Ransford Königsdörffer supplied the final blow in stoppage time.

The result provided an emphatic response to Mainz's somewhat underwhelming goalless draw with SC Paderborn on Matchday 1. More importantly, it offered competitive evidence that much of the optimism surrounding Fischer's squad over the summer may have been justified.

GGFN examined Mainz's extraordinary depth in its 2026/27 Bundesliga preview , with Fischer entering the campaign equipped with multiple viable personnel combinations in defense, midfield and attack. Mainz have conceded just one clear goalscoring opportunity across their opening 180 Bundesliga minutes despite reshuffling the back three.

Fischer backs Mainz principles irrespective of personnel

Fischer made three changes following the Paderborn draw, including two in defense. Stefan Posch and Kacper Potulski entered the back three, while Alexander Schwolow replaced Robin Zentner after the Mainz No. 1 was ruled out with a thigh problem.

Fischer admitted that deploying Posch immediately required some consideration.

"I thought I'd better bring him in earlier than necessary than later," Fischer said of the Austrian international. "He'll be gone during the international break. It is such that I like to adhere to the motto of 'better too early than too late'. I think he did well today as long as he had enough energy."

Posch's return to Mainz itself represents another important part of the club's summer squad construction.

The Austrian initially joined during last season's relegation battle and quickly established himself as an automatic starter in Fischer's back three. GGFN covered Mainz's eventual €4m permanent acquisition of Posch following his successful loan spell .

Sunday marked his first league start since returning permanently. Asked whether changing so much in front of a goalkeeper making his first Bundesliga appearance of the season concerned him, Fischer returned to one of the basic ideas underpinning his work at Mainz.

"That's precisely what one expects," Fischer said. "When it comes to principles, one expects the lads to succeed irrespective of who precisely is lining up. It worked very well today. I did have some concerns that it would be a bit much. But in the end, it was necessary that Poschi found a little rhythm. And when it comes to Schwoli, the No. 2 must be ready if the No. 1 isn't available and I think he did his job well."

Schwolow was scarcely required as a shot-stopper.

Hamburg went an hour without creating a clear opportunity, while the veteran keeper instead contributed with accurately timed long distribution as Mainz repeatedly sought to exploit space behind the hosts.

Becker and Tietz partnership overwhelms Hamburg

That direct element proved particularly effective thanks to the developing relationship between Becker and Tietz. Becker punished Nicolai Remberg's errant pass to open the scoring in the 19th minute after Kaishu Sano immediately released him into space. The Suriname international then provided the low cross from which Phillipp Mwene doubled Mainz's advantage shortly before halftime.

Less than three minutes after the restart, Becker again escaped down the right and squared for Tietz to make it 3-0. The sequence represented another significant milestone in Becker's resurgence under the coach who previously worked with him at Union Berlin.

When Mainz brought Becker back to the Bundesliga last winter, Fischer emphasized the advantages of recruiting a player whose qualities he already knew intimately. GGFN covered Becker's reunion with Fischer and the attacker's belief that the Bundesliga suited him better .

Tietz's contribution has followed a similarly revealing trajectory.

Mainz paid approximately €4m to acquire the striker from Augsburg during last season's relegation battle. His scoring numbers initially remained modest, but his deep drops, physical work, aerial presence and contribution to attacking transitions quickly made him indispensable to Fischer.

Against Hamburg, the statistical return matched the underlying work. Tietz converted Becker's cross for the third before scoring again in the 83rd minute, controlling a long ball and exchanging passes with Jae-sung Lee before firing home from the edge of the penalty area.

Königsdörffer then demonstrated why Mainz's attacking options extend beyond the starting partnership. The former Hamburg forward replaced Becker in the 68th minute and completed the 0-5 rout in stoppage time after racing onto Mwene's forward pass, cutting inside Sebastiaan Bornauw and finishing low into the far corner.

His subsequent celebration in front of his former supporters generated controversy , but the goal itself reinforced one of the more striking observations from Mainz's preseason. Fischer can alter significant parts of his team without necessarily altering its functionality. That applied in defense against Hamburg. It applied between the posts. It also applied when Königsdörffer replaced the outstanding Becker.

In midfield, Mainz's successful retention of Kaishu Sano on transfer deadline day gives Fischer the perfect linchpin to tie everything together. His importance was evident again on Sunday. Sano's interception and immediate vertical pass created the opening goal, setting the tone for a Mainz performance built around intelligent aggression rather than merely dominating possession.

Fischer's Mainz begin to justify summer optimism

The scale of Sunday's victory should naturally be viewed alongside the extent of Hamburg's problems. Fischer's side nevertheless did considerably more than simply capitalize on individual mistakes.

They controlled the opening stages, remained comfortable when HSV enjoyed more harmless possession, attacked vertically when the opportunity presented itself and continued executing with remarkable seriousness after the result had long been decided.

That maturity represents the latest stage in a transformation that began when Fischer inherited a side anchored to the bottom of the Bundesliga last December. Mainz entered this season with very different expectations. The summer brought an unbeaten preseason, significant investment, exceptional depth and the successful retention of Sano.

The question was whether those ingredients would survive the transition into competitive football. After two matches, Fischer's side have four points, five goals and two clean sheets. More revealingly, significant personnel changes have done little to disturb the underlying structure.

For Fischer, that is precisely how it is supposed to work.

articles.title: Bayern CEO shuts down Real Madrid-Michael Olise transfer rumors
articles.summary: Bayern Munich CEO says they never received an offer for their star player.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen recently denied the rumors going around during the latest transfer window regarding a possible exit of star winger Michael Olise. As reported last month, there were some rumors of Olise potentially leaving Der Rekordmeister and of Real Madrid having made an offer for the Frenchman. These notions were even denied by Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez.

Speaking to Sport1-Doppelpass , Dreesen dismissed the rumors regarding the winger. "That simply wasn't true. That's why I said it publicly. It simply wasn't true. We didn't have any offer on the table. And we've always said we weren't interested. That's exactly our position. Olise is incredibly important for this team. He's a magician on this pitch ," stated Dreesen (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Dreesen was then asked for reassurance on the player's status; however, as expected, the CEO avoided making any guarantees on Olise's future. "Making promises is a tricky matter. Whether we can keep him permanently is something we will discuss again in the summer."

A player of his status will always attract the attention of the best teams in Europe, and although nothing is sure in football, at least the Frenchman appears to be content in Munich at the moment.

articles.title: Group of fans kicked out of Portland Thorns NWSL match over pro-women apparel labeled 'transphobic'
articles.summary: Video shows eight fans in XX-XY Athletics gear ejected from a Portland Thorns FC match at Providence Park after LGBTQ organizer lobbied officials.
articles.body: A group of eight people was confronted at their seats and ejected from a Portland Thorns match at Providence Park after stadium security flagged their pro-women apparel. Footage obtained by OutKick shows Amy E. Sousa attempting to speak with a venue staff member for about a minute as the group sat in their assigned seats for the NWSL match against the Washington Spirit. Attendees were wearing gear from XX-XY Athletics alongside shirts bearing slogans such as "Save Women's Sports," "Girls just wanna have fundamental rights," "Woman," and "It's common sense." WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME In the video, venue staff hand the group a card notifying them of an infraction of the Providence Park and NWSL Code of Conduct before escorting them out of the building. The notice gave venue staff 72 hours to contact the group about additional penalties. It also warned that refusing to provide personal information on the spot could lead to a ban from all future events at the stadium. Sousa later told OutKick that she was accused of being transphobic. ADF SENDS LETTER TO WNBA AFTER CONTROVERSIES OVER TREATMENT OF SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS Following the ejection, Sousa took to social media to push back against any claim that the group caused a disturbance inside the venue before security stepped in. "We did nothing. We had not even shown our shirts. We were dressed like this when ejected," Sousa posted on X in response to the incident. WNBA FANS RECALL EJECTION THREAT OVER XX-XY ATHLETICS SHIRT AT FEVER-DREAM GAME: 'I WAS FLABBERGASTED' The episode at Providence Park, which is owned by the City of Portland but operated by a private company, raises questions about how speech rules are enforced at a publicly owned stadium. Fans face a core question: Who polices game-day gear, and when does safety cross into overreach? The incident also highlights a contrast in how Portland’s sports teams handle fan attire. Sousa previously attended a WNBA game at the Moda Center between the Portland Fire and Indiana Fever wearing her XX-XY Athletics shirt. She was even featured on the arena’s massive jumbotron during the live broadcast, while the Thorns later booted Sousa and the other fans from Providence Park for wearing similar pro-women apparel. "I didn't take it seriously," Sousa said regarding online warnings she received before Sunday's match. "I was like, what are they going to do? Arrest us for watching soccer?" SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SHARES TOUCHING MOMENT WITH YOUNG FEVER FAN AFTER GAME AGAINST PORTLAND The security response at Providence Park followed public social media posts from a local LGBT group organizer, Hannah Perry, who lobbied municipal and state officials to intervene at the city-owned stadium. Ahead of game time, Perry fired off a Facebook message to Sousa letting him know she’d already put the Portland PD, the mayor and Gov. Tina Kotek on notice. Perry added that she was contacting Providence Park directly, alongside local organizations, to demand the group be removed. She called Sousa a "pathetic excuse of a human being" and wrote, "I hope that you're not allowed into the stadium." Under the NWSL Fan Code of Conduct, spectators are prohibited from displaying signs, symbols, words or imagery used for political campaigning or advocacy. However, neither the league nor venue rules provide an objective standard for what turns basic slogan apparel into banned political expression, leaving enforcement largely to staff discretion. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Requests for comment sent to Providence Park venue management, Portland Thorns and NWSL league headquarters were not immediately returned. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.body:

Referee: Rodrigo José Pereira de Lima (PE) Assistant 1: Francisco Chaves Bezerra Junior (PE) Assistant 2: Karla Renata Cavalcanti de Santana (PE) 4th official: Fabio Augusto Santos Sá Junior (SE) VAR: Gilberto Rodrigues Castro Junior (PE)

Yellow cards: Arthur Cabral, Marçal, Montoro ( BOTAFOGO ). Alexander Barboza (2), Marlon Freitas (Palmeiras). Red cards: Alexander Barboza (Palmeiras).

BOTAFOGO : Gabriel Batista; Vitinho (Mateo Ponte), Ferraresi, Lucas Monzón and Marçal; Villalba (Júnior Santos), Huguinho, Danilo (Edenilson) and Montoro (Medina); Danilo Pereira and Arthur Cabral (Kadir). Coach: Rodrigo Bellão.

Palmeiras: Carlos Miguel; Giay (Khellven), Gustavo Gómez, Alexander Barboza and Piquerez; Andreas Pereira (Larson), Marlon Freitas and Lucas Evangelista (John Arias); Felipe Anderson (Emiliano Martínez), Maurício (Vitor Roque) and Flaco López. Coach: Abel Ferreira.
